source_refs.quote: upholding the vice of sub-letting without consent of the landlord

law_refs.quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; respondent landlord; unidentified alleged subtenant; unspecified portion of the Delhi building.
tests.opposition: No specific contrary subletting date appears. The precise disposition date is not supplied.
tests.rationale: The appellant became tenant in May 1954. The Controller and Tribunal found subletting by that tenant. A disposition by him as tenant would necessarily postdate 9 June 1952. This supports the temporal proposition at the prior-finding level without establishing the precise transaction date.

source_refs.quote: The Rent Controller, at the floor level, ordered eviction and the Appellate Tribunal affirmed it
upholding the vice of sub-letting without consent of the landlord

law_refs.quote: In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; unidentified purported subtenant; unspecified portion of the premises.
tests.opposition: The supplied excerpts do not separately identify the subtenant, rent payments, transferred estate interest, or precise possession rights.
tests.rationale: The Tribunal expressly upheld the finding of subletting. That finding supports the subletting proposition at the supplied procedural level, although the underlying tenancy incidents are not individually reproduced. It is not elevated to an unseen target determination.

source_refs.quote: unauthorized sub-letting of a portion of the premises

law_refs.quote: In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; unidentified alleged recipient; Delhi building.
tests.opposition: The pleaded and previously adjudicated disposition concerns subletting, not an identified assignment.

opposition_refs.quote: upholding the vice of sub-letting without consent of the landlord

tests.gap_reason: No identified assignment transaction, assignee, or transfer of all tenant rights is supplied.
tests.rationale: The distinct assignment proposition cannot reliably be assessed from a finding of subletting. Absence of an assignment allegation is not treated as affirmative refutation.

source_refs.quote: upholding the vice of sub-letting without consent of the landlord

law_refs.quote: there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; unidentified other person; unspecified premises portion.
tests.opposition: The excerpts provide no independent description of divestment of physical and legal possession.
tests.gap_reason: The purported recipient and actual allocation of legal-possession rights are unidentified.
tests.rationale: A prior finding of subletting is not automatically converted into a separate finding that the tenant relinquished physical possession and the right to possession.

source_refs.quote: upholding the vice of sub-letting without consent of the landlord
there was an express condition against sub-letting

law_refs.quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; respondent landlord; alleged subletting of a portion.
tests.opposition: No affirmative written consent appears in the supplied material. The contractual prohibition is distinct from the statutory written-consent question.
tests.rationale: The Controller and Tribunal upheld subletting without landlord consent. Their finding supports the absence-of-written-consent proposition at that procedural level. The contractual restriction provides additional context but is not itself substituted for the finding.

source_refs.quote: unauthorized sub-letting of a portion of the premises

law_refs.quote: If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; unidentified alleged subtenant; unspecified portion.
tests.opposition: No concurrent-user arrangement, license, or evidence of retained legal possession is described.
tests.gap_reason: The tenant's continuing legal-possession rights concerning the relevant portion are not described.
tests.rationale: The retained-possession qualification cannot be assessed from the general subletting finding. Neither retention nor complete exclusion is inferred merely from the absence of further details.

law_refs.quote: the whole or any part of the premises

tests.objects: Tenant; unidentified alleged subtenant; portion of the let Delhi building.
tests.opposition: The exact portion is not delineated.
tests.rationale: The eviction allegation expressly concerns a portion of the let premises, and the prior courts upheld subletting. The statute encompasses any part of the premises; precise spatial measurements are not needed to identify the supported general proposition.
